title: 1986 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The 1986 FIFA World Cup unfolded across Mexico from 31 May to 29 June, the nation becoming the first to host the tournament twice after previously staging the 1970 edition. Mexico had stepped in when original hosts Colombia withdrew. Twenty-four teams competed, drawn into six groups of four; the top two from each group, together with the four best third-placed sides, advanced to a 16-team knockout phase. This was the first World Cup to use the round of 16 format, followed by quarter-finals, semi-finals, a third-place match, and the final. Matches were contested at high altitude and in heat, several kicking off at noon local time to suit European television audiences. Canada, Denmark, and Iraq all made their tournament debuts. Total attendance reached 2,394,031 across 52 matches, averaging about 46,039 per match.

The tournament belonged to Diego Maradona, who captained and dragged Argentina to the title in what is widely regarded as the greatest individual World Cup campaign. In the quarter-final against England he scored both the 'Hand of God' goal, punched in unseen by officials, and minutes later the 'Goal of the Century', dribbling past several England players from his own half. Across the tournament Maradona scored five goals and provided five assists, a hand in 10 of Argentina's 14 goals, and won the Golden Ball as best player.

France, led by Michel Platini, beat reigning holders Italy 2–0 in the round of 16, then Brazil on penalties (4–3) after a 1–1 draw, before losing to West Germany in the semi-final and taking third place. Belgium reached the semi-finals for the first time, finishing fourth.

The final at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City on 29 June saw Argentina face West Germany. José Luis Brown opened the scoring in the 23rd minute and Jorge Valdano added a second in the 56th. West Germany equalized through Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (74') and Rudi Völler (81'), but Jorge Burruchaga struck the winner in the 84th minute from a Maradona pass. Argentina prevailed 3–2 in normal time to claim a second world title, after 1978. Gary Lineker of England was the tournament's top scorer with six goals.
